title: Verify SpotNodePool autoscaling field names (minNodes/maxNodes) against a live autoscaled pool

comments.author: cli
comments.text:
GAP (Phase 2 residual). internal/spot/types.go header comment (approx lines 6-14) states fixed-pool field names were VERIFIED 2026-07-27 against a live pool, BUT: "Autoscaling min/max field names are still assumed (the sample pool had autoscaling disabled) - confirm the first time an autoscaled pool exists." The sample pool had autoscaling.enabled=false, so minNodes/maxNodes JSON keys were never seen on a real object.

WHY IT MATTERS: two load-bearing paths depend on those unverified keys:
- internal/spot/types.go UpperBound() reads Spec.Autoscaling.MaxNodes for the org-wide ceiling sum (the plan's core invariant #4).
- internal/spot/client.go ScaleNodePool() autoscaled branch patches spec.autoscaling.maxNodes.
If the real CRD key differs (e.g. max_nodes / maximumNodes), the merge-patch silently no-ops (scale appears to succeed but nothing changes) and the ceiling accounting is computed from a zero/missing field - a fail-OPEN hole in an otherwise fail-closed policy. docs/research/rackspace-spot-api.md line 55 also flags these as doc-sourced/unverified.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Do GET spotnodepools on a live pool that has autoscaling.enabled=true in the dedicated org and capture the exact JSON keys for the min/max fields.
- Confirm or correct the json tags on internal/spot/types.go Autoscaling{MinNodes,MaxNodes}.
- Confirm the ScaleNodePool autoscaled patch targets the verified key.
- Update the types.go comment and docs/research/rackspace-spot-api.md to mark autoscaling fields VERIFIED, and tick plan.md Phase 2.

title: Bid-cap default drift: docs say 0.001, code/deploy default is 0.01

comments.author: cli
comments.text:
GAP (documentation drift, plan vs artifacts). Three documents state the bid-cap default is 0.001, but the code and deployment default to 0.01:

Say 0.001:
- docs/plan/plan.md line 82: "P.bidPrice <= maxBid (default 0.001)"
- docs/notes/invariant-policy.md line 13: "Bid cap | 0.001"
- README.md line 31: "Bid cap (default 0.001)"

Actually 0.01:
- internal/config/config.go line 55: env default "0.01"
- deploy/deployment.yaml line 38: WARDEN_MAX_BID_PRICE "0.01" with note "Spot raised the gp.vs1.medium floor to 0.01/hr (was 0.001); verified via serverclasses API 2026-07-27"

ROOT CAUSE: docs/research/rackspace-spot-api.md lines 107 documents that the gp.vs1.medium-iad minimum bid floor moved 0.001 -> 0.01 (10x). The code default was updated; the plan, invariant-policy note, and README were not. A stale documented default here is misleading for an enforcement-envelope value.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Update plan.md line 82, invariant-policy.md line 13, and README.md line 31 to 0.01 (matching config.go / deployment.yaml), with a one-line note that the Spot floor moved 10x.
- Confirm no other doc still cites 0.001 as the enforced cap (the ~$0.001 floor-bid mentions in plan.md line 14 are historical context, not the cap; adjust wording if it now reads inconsistently).

title: No tests for security-critical server/spot/config packages

comments.author: cli
comments.text:
GAP (shipped security-critical code with no tests). go test ./... shows tests exist ONLY for internal/policy; internal/server, internal/spot, and internal/config have "[no test files]". The plan's Phase 1 scoped tests to the "policy engine", but the security model (docs/notes/security-model.md) rests on guarantees that live in the UNtested packages:

- internal/server/server.go: caller auth is the primary access control. lookup() does a constant-time subtle.ConstantTimeCompare over sha256 digests; bearer() parses the header; scalePool() implements the read-before-write flow and the not-found path. None of this is exercised by a test (e.g. missing token -> 401, wrong token -> 401, valid token -> pass, deny -> 403 with no upstream call).
- internal/spot/client.go: ScaleNodePool() is the "patch touches ONLY the count" guarantee (security-model.md control 3) - the fixed vs autoscaled branch builds spec.desired vs spec.autoscaling.maxNodes and must never emit serverClass/bidPrice. This invariant is asserted in prose but not tested. accessToken() also has non-trivial caching/early-refresh and the id_token-vs-access_token selection (a subtle 401 trap documented in the code).
- internal/config/config.go: validate() aggregates required-field / org- prefix / count errors and applies defaults; untested.

WHY IT MATTERS: these are exactly the paths whose failure silently weakens the gateway (auth bypass, or a patch that leaks a disallowed field). They pass vet/build while being unverified.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Add internal/server table tests using httptest: no-bearer 401, unknown-token 401, valid-token allow path, policy-deny returns 403 and does NOT call ScaleNodePool.
- Add internal/spot test asserting the marshaled patch body for fixed vs autoscaled pools contains ONLY the count field (no serverClass/bidPrice), plus a token-caching/refresh test with a stub token endpoint returning id_token.
- Add internal/config tests for validate() (missing refresh token / missing or bad org namespace / empty caller tokens / defaults applied).
- go test ./... green.
